records.title: Ādāmōḍi Gaḷadē
records.meaning: Asks if there is anyone as forgiving and gracious as Sri Rama, who tolerates every fault of his devotees.
records.notes: Popular Charukesi kriti, often used to showcase the raga's characteristic swaras.

records.title: Aḍavāramella Kūḍi
records.pallavi: Adavaramella kudi manamu adudamu Harini vedi
records.meaning: The gopis say to one another: let all of us maidens join together and go speak to Hari, coaxing him to come play with us.
records.notes: Follows the vachana dialogues between the gopis and Krishna early in the play.

records.title: Adigi Sukhamu
records.pallavi: Adigi sukhamu evvarikiraa ee bhoomi lo
records.meaning: The singer questions whether anyone in this world has ever attained the happiness they went looking for through mere worldly pursuit, contrasting it with devotion to Rama.
records.notes: Kalyani kriti reflecting on the futility of seeking happiness in worldly life.

records.title: Aḍugu Varamula
records.meaning: Sung as the Lord's own words to Prahlada: 'Ask, and I shall grant you whatever boons you seek' — the Lord tempts and tests Prahlada's devotion with worldly offers.
records.notes: Kriti no. 18 of Prahlada Bhakti Vijayam in the standard sequence.

records.title: Allakallōlamāyenu
records.meaning: As the storm strikes and the boat begins to founder, the terrified gopis cry that everything has fallen into utter confusion, and pray to Goddess Yamuna to save Krishna and relieve their trouble.
records.notes: The addressee within the song is Yamuna Devi, but the piece belongs to the Krishna-centred Nauka Charitram narrative.

records.title: Anupama Guṇāmbudhi
records.pallavi: Anupama guṇāmbudhi śrī rāmā nīvē gati
records.meaning: Addresses Rama as the boundless ocean of matchless virtues, and the singer's sole refuge.
records.notes: Well-known Atana kriti, frequently taught to intermediate students.

records.title: Bāla Kanaka Maya Cēla
records.pallavi: Bāla kanaka maya cēla dharuni rāma
records.meaning: Describes the young Rama's golden robes and radiant form.
records.notes: Less frequently performed Atana kriti compared to Anupama Gunambudhi.

records.title: Baṇṭu Rīti Kolu
records.pallavi: Baṇṭu rīti kolu swāmi nīvē manasuku telisi
records.meaning: The singer offers himself as Rama's loyal servant, asking to be accepted into faithful service.
records.notes: Extremely popular concert item; one of the best-known Hamsanadam kritis.

records.title: Bhajana Sēyavē
records.meaning: Instructs the mind to simply get on with worship.

records.title: Bhāvanuta Nā Manasu
records.pallavi: Bhāvanuta nā manasu nī vasamā rāma
records.meaning: Asks whether the singer's mind, praised for its devotion, is truly under Rama's control.

records.title: Bhōgīndra Śāyinaṃ
records.meaning: Calls on the mind to worship Vishnu, who reclines upon the serpent couch.
records.notes: One of Tyagaraja's few Sanskrit compositions, set in the rare raga Kuntalavarali.

records.title: Bhuvini Dāsuḍane
records.meaning: Declares oneself a true servant of Rama in this world, questioning the sincerity of that claim.
records.notes: Composed in the ghana raga Sri; less commonly performed.

records.title: Brōva Bhāramā
records.meaning: Asks Rama whether protecting the singer is really too great a burden for him.

records.title: Cakkani Rāja Mārgamu
records.meaning: Compares surrender to Rama's grace to a clear royal road, contrasted with the crooked bylanes of other paths.
records.notes: Concert staple; often taught early for its clear structure.

records.title: Cēdē Buddi Mānurā
records.meaning: Admonishes the mind to abandon its base, harmful thoughts.

records.title: Cēsinadella Maracitivō
records.meaning: Asks Rama if he has forgotten all the good deeds the singer has done for him.

records.title: Chētulārā Śṛṅgāramu
records.pallavi: Chetulara sringaramu seyu vela idera Rama
records.meaning: The singer describes decorating and adorning Rama with his own hands, expressing devotion through the ritual act of decking out the deity.
records.notes: Todi kriti describing devotional adornment of the deity.

records.title: Chinnanāḍēna Nēḍu Chelimi
records.pallavi: Chinnanadena needu chelimi seyu vaadanu kaanu
records.meaning: The devotee protests that his friendship and devotion to Rama did not begin only today, but stretches back through many lifetimes, so the Lord should not now abandon him.
records.notes: Kalyani kriti expressing the singer's long-standing bond with Rama.

records.title: Cūḍarē Celulārā
records.pallavi: Choodare chelulara Yamuna Devi sogasella santoshamuna
records.meaning: The gopis call to one another, 'Look, friends, at the joyous beauty of the river Yamuna!' — describing the cuckoos and the romantic atmosphere on the riverbank before the boat ride.

records.title: Dācukōvalenā
records.meaning: Asks why one should have to hide one's devotion in the presence of those who lack compassion.
records.notes: Major Todi concert piece, technically demanding.

records.title: Dārini Telusukoṇṭi
records.meaning: Says he has found the way, addressing the Goddess Tripurasundari of Tiruvottiyur.
records.notes: From the Tiruvoṭṭiyūr set on Devi — unusual for a composer whose work is almost entirely on Rama.

records.title: Dāśarathī Nī Ṛṇamu
records.meaning: The singer laments being unable to repay the debt of gratitude owed to Dasarathi (Rama).

records.title: Daya Sēyavayya
records.meaning: Prahlada pleads with the merciful Lord to grant him the same comfort and devotion that Sita drew from contemplating the Lord's grace.
records.notes: Raga and narrative context are well attested; the tala (given here as Adi) is less firmly confirmed than for the other Prahlada Bhakti Vijayam entries.

records.title: Dinamaṇi Vaṃśa
records.meaning: Praises Rama as the moon risen from the nectarous ocean that is the Solar dynasty.

records.title: Dorakunā Ituvaṇṭi Sēva
records.meaning: Wonders whether such an opportunity to serve Rama will ever come again.

records.title: Dorakunāyani Sūrula
records.meaning: Indra, lord of the celestials, sets out wondering whether he might be privileged to behold Hari, moon-faced with Sita by his side, being worshipped by Prahlada.

records.title: Duḍukugala Nannē
records.pallavi: Duḍukugala nannē dora koḍuku brōcurā entō
records.meaning: Tyagaraja calls himself a wretch full of misdeeds and asks which prince's son would trouble to save him — a catalogue of self-accusation.
records.notes: The charanams are an unsparing list of the composer's own failings. Gaula's vakra descent makes this the hardest of the five to keep in tune.

records.title: Ēlā Nī Daya Rādu
records.pallavi: Ēlā nī daya rādu rāmā nāpai
records.meaning: Asks Rama why his compassion has still not descended upon the singer.
records.notes: Aṭāṇā (also spelt Aṭana) is a rakti rāga where the gāndhāra is heavily oscillated — the scale on paper tells you very little about it.

records.title: Ēmani Vinnavintura
records.pallavi: Emani vinnavintura nannu brova ide vela ika
records.meaning: The devotee asks what more he can possibly submit to Rama in supplication, declaring that now is the very moment for the Lord to come and protect him.
records.notes: A well-loved kriti in the rakti raga Ritigaula, frequently performed as a main item.

records.title: Ēmi Jēsitēnēmi
records.meaning: Declares that whatever one does is fruitless without purity of mind.

records.title: Endarō Mahānubhāvulu
records.meaning: Salutes the countless great souls who have realised the divine — the composer bowing to everyone who came before him.
records.notes: Always sung last of the five, and the piece that closes the massed Ārādhana rendition at Tiruvaiyāru. Śrī rāga's narrow contours make the swara passages deceptively hard.

records.title: Endu Dāginādō
records.meaning: Wonders where Rama is hiding, unseen by his devotee.

records.title: Endukū Peddala
records.meaning: Questions why the young do not heed the counsel of their elders.

records.title: Enta Muddō
records.pallavi: Enta muddō enta sogasō śrī rāma bāla
records.meaning: Describes how utterly charming and beautiful the child Rama appears.
records.notes: Popular vatsalya-bhava (parental-love) kriti depicting baby Rama.

records.title: Ēṭāvunarā
records.meaning: Asks what manner of person withholds compassion, questioning Rama's delay in showing grace.

records.title: Ēṭi Janma Midi
records.pallavi: Ēṭi janma midi rāma bhakti lēka
records.meaning: Laments what kind of birth this is, lived without devotion to Rama.
records.notes: Set in Varali, one of the ghana ragas; demanding, ancient raga.

records.title: Ēṭula Brōtuvō
records.meaning: Wonders in what way Rama will ultimately choose to protect the singer.

records.title: Ēvari Māṭa Vinnavēmirā
records.meaning: Asks the mind whose advice it has been listening to, having strayed from devotion.

records.title: Evarichchirirā Ī Ānanda
records.meaning: Tyagaraja asks who else could have given him this bliss, other than the Lord himself, celebrating the joy that devotion has brought him.
records.notes: Sahana kriti expressing the bliss (ananda) of devotion.

records.title: Evaru Manaku Samānamu
records.meaning: The gopis boast to one another, in their pride, that no one on earth today is equal to them now that Krishna has become theirs — the very pride the boat episode is designed to humble.
records.notes: Listed as kriti no. 11 of the Nauka Charitram sequence; a madhyama-kala composition.

records.title: Gandhamu Puyyarugā
records.meaning: The gopis, meeting Krishna joyfully at the riverbank, apply sandal paste to him, expressing their devotion in service before pride sets in and the boat trip turns dangerous.

records.title: Giripai Nelakonna
records.meaning: Describes Lord Venkatesa, who has made his abode atop the hill.
records.notes: Popular Venkatesa kriti associated with Tirumala.

records.title: Grahabalamēmi
records.meaning: Declares that planetary influence means nothing when Rama himself is one's strength.

records.title: Hari Hari Nī(y)okka
records.meaning: The chastened gopis beg Krishna, 'Hari, Hari, grant us your holy feet' realising that worldly pleasure and fortune are not permanent, and seeking refuge in surrender.
records.notes: The 14th piece of Nauka Charitram, sung after the boat begins to sink, as the gopis' pride gives way to surrender.

records.title: Heccarikagā Rārā
records.meaning: Calls Rama to come forth watchfully, alert to the devotee's plea.

records.title: Ī Vasudha Nīvaṇṭi
records.pallavi: Ee vasudha nivanti daya galavarevaru kanamu
records.meaning: Asks where in this world one could find a god as compassionate as Siva of Kovur, who bestows boons and causes all growth and prosperity.
records.notes: Composed June 1839 at the Sundareswara temple, Kovur, during its Vaisakha Visakham festival; one of the five Kovur Pancharatna kritis.

records.title: Inta Saukhyamanine
records.meaning: Exclaims that no one else can be told of such happiness found in devotion to Rama.

records.title: Intakannānandamēmi
records.meaning: Asks what greater joy exists than chanting the name of Rama.

records.title: Jagadānandakāraka
records.meaning: Hails Rama as the source of the world's joy and the lord of Janaki's life — the only Pancharatna entirely in Sanskrit.
records.notes: Ten charanams, each a garland of Rama's names in Sanskrit. The one Pancharatna with no Telugu in it. Learn the pallavi and one charanam properly before attempting the whole.

records.title: Jñānamosaga Rādā
records.meaning: Pleads with Rama to grant the wisdom needed for liberation.

records.title: Jō Jō Rāma Ānanda
records.meaning: A lullaby in which Tyagaraja, adopting the voice of a mother, sings Rama to sleep, repeating the sleep-refrain 'jo jo' while praising the Lord's qualities and form; sung at the pavalimpu (putting-to-rest) part of the daily ritual.
records.notes: Ritigaula's gently rocking arohana/avarohana suits the lullaby mood; one of Tyagaraja's best-known pavalimpu songs.

records.title: Kaddanuvāriki
records.meaning: Speaks of being unable to refuse those who claim to belong to oneself.

records.title: Kalyāṇamu Vaibhōgamē
records.meaning: Celebrates the splendour of Rama and Sita's wedding — sung at the marriage sequence of temple festivals.
records.notes: A ritual song for the kalyāṇōtsavam; the tala is written as khaṇḍa cāpu but many groups sing it in a relaxed Adi.

records.title: Kanakana Rucirā
records.meaning: The more he looks at the golden-robed Rama, the sweeter the sight becomes — a kriti built entirely on the pleasure of darshan.
records.notes: Varāḷi is traditionally not taught guru-to-student directly; learners pick it up by listening. Take the vakra ārōhaṇa slowly.

records.title: Kanna Talli Nīvu
records.meaning: Addresses the Goddess as 'my own birth-mother', asking that the good fortune of her grace fall to the singer's share.
records.notes: One of the five Tiruvottiyur Pancharatna kritis on Devi Tripurasundari; composed for Veena Kuppayyar.

records.title: Karuṇājaladhi
records.meaning: Calls Rama the ocean of compassion, pleading to be governed and protected by him.

records.title: Koluvaiyunnāḍē
records.meaning: Announces that Lord Rama is present, holding court, ready to receive his devotees.

records.title: Koluvamaregadā
records.meaning: Asks Rama why he no longer holds court to receive his devotees, having hidden himself away.
records.notes: Landmark Todi masterpiece, a concert staple demanding advanced technique.

records.title: Kōri Sēvimparārē
records.meaning: Invites devotees to lovingly seek out and serve Sundareswara, the Lord of Kovur, consort of Goddess Saundarya Nayaki.
records.notes: One of the five Kovur Pancharatna kritis; four of the five have only a single charanam.

records.title: Kṣīṇamai Tiruganu
records.meaning: The singer, worn down and weakened, asks whom else he can implore for help.

records.title: Kṣīra Sāgara Śayana
records.pallavi: Ksheera sagara sayana sri Rama nannu brova
records.meaning: The singer addresses Rama as the one who reclines on the ocean of milk (identifying him with Vishnu/Adisesha-Narayana) and pleads with him to come and protect the devotee.
records.notes: Devagandhari kriti identifying Rama with the reclining Vishnu of the Ksheerasagara.

records.title: Kṣīra Sāgara Vihāra
records.pallavi: Kshira sagara vihara aparimita ghora pataka vidara
records.meaning: Addresses the Lord as the one who sports in the ocean of milk (Vishnu reclining on Adisesha) and who tears apart even the most terrible sins of his devotees.
records.notes: Grouped with the utsava-sampradaya kirtanas in the standard published collection.

records.title: Lāli Yugavē Māpāli Daivama
records.meaning: A cradle/swing lullaby: 'Oh our own Lord, sway gently (on the swing/cradle), lali' — sung while rocking the deity, praising Rama's qualities in each charanam.
records.notes: Neelambari is the traditional lullaby raga in Carnatic music; this is Tyagaraja's principal unjal/pavalimpu song in it.

records.title: Mā Jānaki Chettabaṭṭi
records.meaning: The kriti recalls the moment Rama, holding Sita's (Janaki's) hand, releases the Brahmastra, celebrating his valour and devotion to Sita in the same breath.
records.notes: Narrative kriti recalling a scene from the Ramayana war episode.

records.title: Mānasā Etulō
records.meaning: Tyagaraja tells his own mind not to keep a distant, half-hearted friendship with the Lord, urging it toward whole-hearted devotion.
records.notes: Self-addressed kriti in the rare raga Malayamarutam.

records.title: Mānasu Svādhīnamaina
records.meaning: Tyagaraja declares that for one who has gained mastery over his own mind, nothing at all remains difficult to achieve.
records.notes: Popular Sankarabharanam kriti on mastery of the mind as the key to spiritual attainment.

records.title: Marakata Maṇimaya
records.meaning: The kriti describes Rama's dark, emerald-hued splendour, comparing his complexion and radiance to the lustre of a marakata (emerald) gem.
records.notes: Rare-raga kriti in the gentle, lullaby-like raga Nilambari.

records.title: Mari Mari Ninnē
records.meaning: Again and again he has pleaded — and asks how many more times he must.

records.title: Marugēlarā
records.meaning: Why the concealment, Raghava? — asks why Rama hides himself from one who has no other refuge.
records.notes: Jayantasēna is used for almost nothing else, so the rāga and the kriti are learnt together.

records.title: Mēlukōvaiyya
records.meaning: A suprabhatam-style waking song asking Rama to rise from sleep at dawn, part of the Utsava Sampradaya kritis composed for daily temple worship.
records.notes: One of Tyagaraja's Utsava Sampradaya Kirtanas used in ritual temple worship of Rama's daily routine.

records.title: Mēru Samāna
records.meaning: Praises Rama as steady as Mount Meru.
records.notes: One of the few concert kritis in Māyāmāḷavagauḷa, the rāga every student begins with in varisai practice.

records.title: Mōkṣamu Galadā
records.pallavi: Mōkṣamu galadā bhuvilō jīvanmuktulu gāni vāralaku
records.meaning: Asks whether liberation is possible at all for those who are not already free while living — and answers that music itself is the path.
records.notes: The charanam names bhakti, saṅgīta and jñāna together. Sāramati's four-note descent is what makes the piece sound like it is looking inward.

records.title: Muripemu Kaligina
records.meaning: The kriti speaks of the tender affection a child receives standing before a doting mother, using this image as a metaphor for the devotee's relationship with the Lord.
records.notes: Set in the rakti raga Kanada.

records.title: Nā Jīvādhāra
records.meaning: Calls Rama the very support of his life, then asks why he is being ignored.

records.title: Nā Moralanu Vinarāda
records.meaning: The devotee asks Rama why he will not listen to his earnest pleas and cries of distress.
records.notes: Supplication kriti in Kambhoji; pathantaram details vary between renditions.

records.title: Nādalōluḍai
records.meaning: Tyagaraja describes how the mind that is absorbed in nada (sacred sound/music) becomes established in Brahmananda, the bliss of the Absolute, making the case that music itself is a path to liberation.
records.notes: One of Tyagaraja's core nada-upasana kritis, in the grand raga Kalyani.

records.title: Nādōpāsana Chēse
records.pallavi: Nadopasana chese vaariki dorakani sukhamu koladu
records.meaning: Tyagaraja proclaims that for those who worship God through nada (sacred sound), there is no limit to the happiness they attain, reiterating his conviction that music itself is a spiritual path.
records.notes: Another central nada-upasana statement kriti, in Begada raga.

records.title: Nāḍupai Baluka Vēmira
records.meaning: The devotee asks Rama why he continues to delay in speaking or responding, expressing impatience born of deep longing.
records.notes: Kriti of impatient longing, set in raga Nayaki.

records.title: Nagumōmu Galavāni
records.meaning: Longs for one glimpse of the smiling-faced Lord who has stolen his heart, and asks Garuda to carry the message.
records.notes: Probably the single most-performed Tyagaraja kriti. The anupallavi asks Garuda why he has not brought Rama — that address is the emotional hinge of the piece.

records.title: Nammi Vaccina Nannu
records.meaning: 'Kindly protect me, who has come to you trusting in you' — Tyagaraja prays for the grace of Sundareswara of Kovur.
records.notes: One of the five Kovur Pancharatna kritis.

records.title: Nannu Pālimpa
records.meaning: Asks whether Rama has actually walked all this way just to look after him.
records.notes: Mōhanaṃ with no half-notes at all — one of the safest first concert pieces, and still substantial enough for swaram.

records.title: Nannu Viḍaci
records.meaning: Begs Rama not to move a step away and leave him behind.
records.notes: Rītigauḷa is all curves and no straight lines; this kriti is the usual vehicle for learning them. Miśra cāpu keeps the phrases from settling.

records.title: Nārada Muni Veḍalina
records.meaning: Describes sage Narada setting out, praised for his outstanding virtues, to bring Prahlada the news of Hari's impending visit.
records.notes: The melody stays largely in the upper (tara) shadja register, characteristic of this rendering of Pantuvarali.

records.title: Nēnendu Vedukudurā
records.pallavi: Nenendu vedukudura needanu vina O Rama
records.meaning: The singer asks where he should search for Rama, when there is nothing besides the Lord himself to look for or find comfort in.
records.notes: Sahana kriti of searching, longing devotion.

records.title: Nī Bhajana Gāna
records.pallavi: Nī bhajana gāna rasikula nīvē kāvavē
records.meaning: Asks Rama to protect those who take delight in singing his praise.

records.title: Nī Daya Rādā
records.pallavi: Nee daya rada ika nannu brova Rama
records.meaning: The devotee asks Rama why his compassion has not yet arrived, pleading for the Lord's grace to protect him now.
records.notes: A plea-for-grace kriti in the springtime raga Vasanta.

records.title: Nī Nāma Rūpamulaku
records.pallavi: Nee naama roopamulaku nitya jaya mangalam
records.meaning: 'Eternal victory and auspiciousness to your sacred name and form' — the closing mangalam that ends Prahlada Bhakti Vijayam and is often sung as a benedictory finale in concerts.
records.notes: The final number of the opera, in the same Saurashtram raga used to open its Ganapati invocation.

records.title: Nidhi Cāla Sukhamā
records.pallavi: Nidhi cāla sukhamā rāmuni sannidhi sēva sukhamā
records.pallavi_telugu: నిధి చాల సుఖమా రాముని సన్నిధి సేవ సుఖమా
records.meaning: Which is the real comfort — a hoard of wealth, or standing in Rama's presence? Written when Tyagaraja refused the Tanjore court's patronage.
records.notes: The biographical kriti: his answer to the king's invitation. Short, and the whole argument sits in the pallavi.

records.title: Ninnē Bhajana
records.meaning: A vow to worship no one but Rama.

records.title: Ō Raṅgaśāyī
records.meaning: Calls out to Ranganatha at Srirangam and asks why, when called, he does not answer.
records.notes: Composed at the Srirangam temple gate. A full-length Kāmbhōji main piece — the charanam's madhyama-kāla passage is the famous stretch.

records.title: Ōḍanu Jaripē Muccaṭa
records.meaning: Describes the delightful spectacle of Krishna and the gopis setting the boat afloat and rowing out onto the river Yamuna.
records.notes: A frequently performed standalone excerpt from Nauka Charitram.

records.title: Palukavadēmirā
records.pallavi: Palukavademira Rama palume na yeda bayalu
records.meaning: The singer implores Rama to speak to him, asking why the Lord remains silent while his devotee's heart is laid bare in longing.
records.notes: A well-known kriti in the rakti raga Saramati.

records.title: Paramātmuḍu Veligē
records.meaning: Says the supreme self shines in everything — in every creature, in every element — and asks the listener to grasp it properly.
records.notes: The most explicitly advaitic of the well-known kritis. Vāgadhīśvari (34th mēḷa) is almost unused elsewhere.

records.title: Patiki Maṅgaḷa Hāratīrē
records.pallavi: Patiki mangala haratire, Sri Ramapatiki mangala haratire
records.meaning: A harati (waving of lamps) song calling on devotees to perform the auspicious lamp-offering to Rama, the Lord of Sita; sung during the harati portion of the daily utsava ritual.
records.notes: A standard harati kriti from the utsava-sampradaya set, distinct from the similarly-titled 'Patiki Harati' in Surati.

records.title: Rāgasudhārasa
records.pallavi: Rāgasudhārasa pānamu jēsi rājillavē ō manasā
records.meaning: Urges the mind to drink the nectar of rāga and shine — devotion through music rather than ritual.
records.notes: One of the nāda-upāsana group where Tyagaraja argues that music is itself the sādhana. Āndōḷikā rocks gently, which suits the argument.

records.title: Raghunāyaka Nannu Brōva
records.pallavi: Raghunayaka nannu brova naa yeda deenudanu ika
records.meaning: The singer calls out to Rama, chief of the Raghu dynasty, describing himself as a helpless soul and asking to be protected.
records.notes: A frequently performed kriti in the compact pentatonic-flavoured raga Hamsanadam.

records.title: Raghupatē Rāma
records.meaning: A garland of epithets addressed to Rama — 'Peerless Lord', 'Lord well sung by Narada', 'Adornment of the Solar dynasty', 'Breaker of Siva's bow' — sung as a devotional name-litany.
records.notes: Raga (Sahana) is well attested; the tala is inferred from the typical medium-paced setting of Tyagaraja's Sahana pieces rather than directly confirmed.

records.title: Rāju Vēḍale
records.pallavi: Raju vedale Kausalya thanaya Ramaraju vedale
records.meaning: The kriti describes the king (Rama, son of Kausalya) setting out in procession, part of the set of Utsava Sampradaya songs describing ceremonial temple events.
records.notes: Utsava Sampradaya processional kriti set to the less common Khanda Chapu tala.

records.title: Rāma Bhakti Sāmrājya
records.meaning: Calls devotion to Rama an empire in itself — the only sovereignty worth holding.

records.title: Rāma Kathā Sudhā
records.meaning: Drinking the nectar of Rama's story is worth more, he says, than any other draught.
records.notes: Madhyamāvati is traditionally a closing rāga, so this often ends a concert.

records.title: Rāma Nannu Brōvarā
records.meaning: A plain, direct appeal: protect me, prince Rama.

records.title: Rāma Nī Samānam Evaru
records.pallavi: Rāma nī samānam evaru raghuvaṃśa sudhāmbudhi candra
records.pallavi_telugu: రామ నీ సమానమెవరు రఘువంశ సుధాంబుధి చంద్ర
records.meaning: Asks who could possibly equal Rama, moon of the nectar-ocean of the Raghu line.
records.notes: The standard Kharaharapriya main piece for students — long enough to carry niraval and swaram, plain enough that the rāga stays audible.

records.title: Rāma Ninnē Nammiti
records.meaning: The devotee declares to Rama that he has placed his trust in the Lord alone, and no one else, asking to be looked after on that basis.
records.notes: Surrender-themed kriti in Harikambhoji.

records.title: Rē Mānasa Cintaya Śrī Rāmam
records.meaning: Tyagaraja addresses his own mind, urging it: 'O mind, ever meditate on Sri Rama' — a simple name-contemplation piece typical of the Divya Nama repertoire.
records.notes: Cited alongside simpler pieces like 'Dasaratha Nandana' as an example of the Divya Nama Kirtana group, though musically somewhat more elaborate than the plainest name-chants.

records.title: Sādhiñcanē
records.meaning: Tells the mind that Rama got his way — a half-affectionate complaint that the Lord always does exactly as he pleases.
records.notes: Famous for its tone: the composer scolds Rama through the charanams, ending with the line about Yasoda. Ārabhi's clean lines expose any slack in the tala.

records.title: Sāmaja Vara Gamana
records.pallavi: Sāmaja vara gamana sādhu hṛt sārasābja pālita
records.meaning: Praises the Lord whose gait is majestic as an elephant's, who tends the lotus-hearts of the good.
records.notes: Sanskrit sāhityam, Hindōḷaṃ's five notes, and a tune that sits comfortably — which is why it turns up in almost every student's first concert set.

records.title: Śāmbhō Mahādēva
records.meaning: Salutes Siva as the great god, consort of Girija.
records.notes: Pantuvarāḷi here is the modern name for the 51st mēḷa Kāmavardhini — not the 45th mēḷa Śubhapantuvarāḷi.

records.title: Saṅgīta Jñānamu Bhakti Vinā
records.pallavi: Sangeeta jnanamu bhakti vina sanmargamu galada
records.meaning: Tyagaraja asks whether there can be any true path to righteousness without musical knowledge joined to devotion, asserting that sangita gyanamu and bhakti are inseparable.
records.notes: A key nada/sangita-upasana statement kriti, set in the melakarta-janya raga Dhenuka.

records.title: Sārasa Sāma Dāna
records.pallavi: Sārasa sāma dāna bhēda daṇḍa catura
records.meaning: Praises Rama as adept in all four instruments of statecraft — conciliation, gifts, division and force.
records.notes: One of the rare kritis whose imagery is political rather than devotional. Kāpī Nārāyaṇi should not be confused with Kāpi.

records.title: Sītamma Māyamma
records.pallavi: Sītamma māyamma śrī rāmuḍu mā taṇḍri
records.meaning: Sita is our mother and Rama our father — the household framing that makes this one of the most-loved of the festival kirtanas.
records.notes: Short, warm and almost always the first utsava sampradāya kīrtana a student learns.

records.title: Śōbhanē Śōbhanē
records.meaning: A benedictory 'sobhanam' song of the kind sung by women during harati/auspicious ceremonies, wishing splendour and well-being to the Lord; part of the utsava-sampradaya festive repertoire.
records.notes: Raga and tala are well attested; its exact place among the utsava ritual sequence (likely the wedding/harati group) is less certain than for the other entries here.

records.title: Śōbhillu Saptasvara
records.meaning: Tells the mind to worship the seven beautiful swaras, which shine in the navel, heart, throat, tongue and nose.
records.notes: A kriti about music itself — it names where each svara resonates in the body. Common early-concert opener.

records.title: Sogasu Jūḍa Taramā
records.pallavi: Sogasu jūḍa taramā nī sogasu jūḍa taramā
records.meaning: Asks whether it is even possible to take in the Lord's beauty — the eye cannot hold it.
records.notes: Commonly listed in Kannaḍagauḷa; some editions place it in Kānaḍā, and the two are handled here under one reference entry. Worth confirming with your teacher.

records.title: Sogasugā Mṛdaṅga Tāḷamu
records.pallavi: Sogasuga mridanga talamu jatiyu sadhukagarada o manasa
records.meaning: Tyagaraja asks his own mind whether it can keep the beautiful rhythm of the mridangam and the jati in tune while singing of Rama, using the joy of rhythm as a metaphor for disciplined devotion.
records.notes: Frequently cited as Tyagaraja's tribute to rhythm and percussion; addressed to his own mind (manasa).

records.title: Śrī Gaṇapatini Sēvimparārē
records.meaning: Urges the mind to worship Lord Ganapati, the remover of obstacles.

records.title: Śrī Nārada
records.meaning: Salutes Narada as the bee at the lotus of nāda — the sage who gave Tyagaraja his music.
records.notes: Tyagaraja composed several kritis on Narada after receiving the Svārārṇava text; this is the best known. Kānaḍā is learnt by imitation, not from its scale.

records.title: Śrī Raghuvara Aprameya
records.meaning: The composer salutes Rama, the best of the Raghu clan, as immeasurable and beyond ordinary comprehension.
records.notes: Kambhoji kriti in Rupaka tala praising Rama's incomparability.

records.title: Śrī Raghuvara Sugunālaya
records.meaning: Addresses Rama as the dwelling-place of every good quality.
records.notes: A weighty Bhairavi piece; good practice ground for the rāga's D2-in-ascent, D1-in-descent asymmetry.

records.title: Śrī Rāma Jaya Rāma
records.pallavi: Śrī rāma jaya rāma śṛṅgāra rāma
records.meaning: A name-chant on Rama in his beauty — built for a group to sing together, not for solo display.
records.notes: Typical divya nāma construction: a short repeating tune, the work carried by the names rather than by melodic variation.

records.title: Śrī Subrahmaṇyāya Namastē
records.meaning: Salutations to Subrahmanya — one of Tyagaraja's handful of Sanskrit kritis on a deity other than Rama.
records.notes: A substantial Kāmbhōji piece; often taken as the main item, with the anupallavi's madhyama-kāla passage as the highlight.

records.title: Śṛṅgārin̄cukoni Vedalirī
records.meaning: Opening daru of Nauka Charitram, describing the gopis dressing and adorning themselves in excitement before setting out to meet Krishna for the boat ride.
records.notes: One of the more frequently excerpted songs from Nauka Charitram in concerts.

records.title: Sujana Jīvana
records.meaning: Rama is the very life of good people.
records.notes: Khamās sits low and warm; this is a common second-item choice.

records.title: Sundara Daśaratha Nandana Vandanamu
records.meaning: 'Salutations to the handsome son of King Dasaratha' — the charanams go on to describe Sita seated gracefully on Rama's lap and the sages Agastya, Vasishtha, Markandeya and others extolling his glory.
records.notes: A dvi-matu keertana: the pallavi has its own tune while all six charanams share a second, common tune, making it well suited to group singing. Distinct from the similarly-named 'Dasaratha Nandana' in raga Asaveri.

records.title: Sundarataraṁ Dēhaṁ
records.meaning: Tyagaraja marvels at the extraordinarily beautiful form of Rama, dwelling on the physical loveliness of the Lord as an object of meditation.
records.notes: A gentle, melodic Madhyamavati kriti describing Rama's beauty.

records.title: Sundarēśvaruni
records.meaning: Praises Lord Siva as Sundareswara ('the beautiful Lord') of Kovur, calling devotees to his worship.
records.notes: One of the five Kovur Pancharatna kritis; the exact opening words of the pallavi beyond the title are not fully confirmed.

records.title: Sundari Nannindarilō
records.meaning: Tyagaraja sings the praises of Goddess Tripurasundari of Tiruvottiyur, singling himself out among all as her devotee.
records.notes: One of the five Tiruvottiyur Pancharatna kritis on Devi Tripurasundari.

records.title: Sundari Nī Divya Rūpamunu
records.meaning: Tyagaraja sings of beholding the Goddess Tripurasundari's divine form at Tiruvottiyur (Adipuram), lost in wonder at her beauty.
records.notes: One of the five Tiruvottiyur Pancharatna kritis on Devi Tripurasundari.

records.title: Sundari Ninnu Varṇimpa
records.meaning: Praises the beautiful Goddess Tripurasundari of Tiruvottiyur, comparing her face to the moon and her splendour to lightning, saying it is beyond words to describe her fully.
records.notes: Composed at the request of his disciple Veena Kuppayyar during a visit to Tiruvottiyur; one of the five Tiruvottiyur Pancharatna kritis on Devi Tripurasundari.

records.title: Teliyalēru Rāma
records.meaning: Says that people cannot recognise the path of devotion, however much they argue about it.
records.notes: Dhēnuka (9th mēḷa) is otherwise barely used; this kriti is effectively the rāga's calling card.

records.title: Tera Tīyagarādā
records.meaning: Asks Venkataramana of Tirupati to draw aside the curtain — outwardly the temple screen, inwardly the veil of ego.
records.notes: The double meaning of "tera" — temple curtain and the veil of the ego — is the whole kriti. Commonly listed in Gauḷipantu; some editions give Gauḷa, and the reference entry here is Gauḷa.

records.title: Uṇḍēdi Rāmuḍokaḍu
records.meaning: There is only one Rama — a flat statement of exclusive devotion.

records.title: Upachāramu Chēsēvāramu
records.meaning: Tyagaraja laments that there is no one left to attend upon and serve the Lord with proper ritual care, expressing the loneliness of true devotion in a careless world.
records.notes: Bhairavi kriti lamenting the scarcity of true devotees.

records.title: Vaddayuṇḍēdē
records.meaning: Prahlada expresses his one-pointed longing to remain always at the Lotus-eyed Lord's side, calling that alone the greatest good.

records.title: Vandanamu Raghunandana
records.meaning: Salutations to the delight of the Raghus, who bridged the sea.
records.notes: Sahānā's gamakas are the point here — sung plainly the kriti loses its character entirely.

records.title: Vara Līla Gāna Lōla
records.pallavi: Vara līla gāna lōla sura pāla suguṇa jāla
records.meaning: Praises the Lord absorbed in the song of his own play — a Sanskrit kriti dense with internal rhyme.

records.title: Vāridhi Nīku
records.meaning: Prahlada, cast into the sea by Hiranyakashipu, salutes the Lord of the Ocean and asks him to show the path by which Hari always dwells in his heart.
records.notes: One of the better-known Todi excerpts from Prahlada Bhakti Vijayam.

records.title: Vāsudēvayani
records.meaning: Draws attention to the Lord's gatekeepers (dvarapalakas) who set out chanting the name 'Vasudeva', heralding the Lord's approach in the Prahlada narrative.

records.title: Vinatasuta Vāhana
records.meaning: The kriti addresses the Lord as one whose mount is the son of Vinata (Garuda), praising his majesty as he is borne through the skies on the eagle-vehicle.
records.notes: Set in the comparatively less common raga Jayantasena.

records.title: Vinavē Ō Manasā
records.pallavi: Vinave o manasa vinu ninnu vina
records.meaning: Tyagaraja addresses his own mind, urging it to listen and understand that there is nothing beside the Lord worth attending to.
records.notes: A self-addressed (manasa) kriti in the less common raga Devamanohari.

records.title: Vināyakuni Valenu Brōva
records.pallavi: Vinayakuni valenu brova vedalitivo Rama nannu
records.meaning: The singer asks whether Rama has come forth to protect him the way he protects through the grace of Vinayaka (Ganesha), invoking Ganesha as the remover of obstacles before praising Rama.
records.notes: A commonly taught Ganesha-invoking kriti of Tyagaraja in the beginner-friendly raga Madhyamavati.

records.title: Yōcanā Kamala Lōcanā
records.meaning: Asks the lotus-eyed one what thought is holding him back from granting his devotee.
